nouveautes.titre: High-dose versus standard-dose liposomal amphotericin B for initial treatment of cerebral mucormycosis: a multicenter target trial emulation.
nouveautes.resume: We emulated a target trial comparing high-dose (>6mg/kg/day) versus standard-dose (≤6mg/kg/day) liposomal amphotericin B in 48 patients with cerebral mucormycosis. High-dose therapy was estimated to increase 42-day survival by 33-percentage-points (95%CI: 9-57), but an increase in toxicity-related discontinuations could not be excluded. Estimate imprecision and residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation.

P. vivax forms hypnozoites, dormant forms of the parasite in the liver that can become reactivated after a few months or even years, causing relapse malaria and enhancing transmission. Therefore, targeting antigens expressed during the pre-erythrocytic stages offers the potential to prevent clinical malaria from both primary and relapse infections.
